title: Coherent nerves of simplicial operator and string categories
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Use the ordinary and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Use simplicial categories and their coherent nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. A nonsymmetric simplicial multicategory $P$ has a small set of colors, simplicial operation sets $P(c_1,\ldots,c_n;d)$ for every finite ordered input list (including $n=0$), and associative unital substitution maps. Suppose every operation set is Kan. Its category of operators $P^\otimes$ has objects finite lists of colors and mapping sets
$$P^\otimes((c_1,\ldots,c_n),(d_1,\ldots,d_m))=\coprod_{\phi:[m]\to[n]}\prod_{i=1}^mP(c_{\phi(i-1)+1},\ldots,c_{\phi(i)};d_i),$$
with composition by substitution and projection to $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Then $N_{\mathrm{hc}}P^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operad; its fiber at $[1]$ is the coherent nerve of the unary simplicial category of $P$.

For any small locally Kan simplicial category $C$, let $D(C)$ have objects $(c_0,\ldots,c_n)$ and mapping sets
$$D(C)((c_0,\ldots,c_n),(d_0,\ldots,d_m))=\coprod_{\phi:[m]\to[n]}\prod_{i=0}^m C(c_{\phi(i)},d_i).$$
Its coherent nerve is the cocartesian fibration over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ classified by $[n]\mapsto(N_{\mathrm{hc}}C)^{n+1}$, with projections and diagonals as transition functors. These identifications are natural in simplicial functors. In particular, for a locally Kan simplicial groupoid it is a left fibration, and its $[n]$ fiber is $(N_{\mathrm{hc}}C)^{n+1}$.

source.place: Definitions 3.1.6–3.1.7 and Lemma 3.1.8; Definition 4.2.2 and Proposition 4.2.3 (the fiber is the (n+1)-fold power, as also in Remark 4.1.2). Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: All indices $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ in the displayed coproducts are order-preserving maps in $\Delta$; their opposites are the projected arrows. In $P^\otimes$, compose operations $(p_j)$ over $\phi$ with $(q_k)$ over $\psi:[\ell]\to[m]$ by substituting $p_{\psi(k-1)+1},\ldots,p_{\psi(k)}$ into $q_k$. The resulting input block runs from $\phi\psi(k-1)+1$ through $\phi\psi(k)$, exactly the block for $\phi\psi$. Each zero-arity entry is the nullary operation carried by the morphism being composed; if its operation space is empty, no morphism requiring that entry exists. No additional nullary operation is chosen. Unary units give identities, and associativity is substitution associativity, with unused end blocks discarded by projections. In $D(C)$ the corresponding composite has $k$th component $g_k\circ f_{\psi(k)}$ and base map $\phi\psi$. The unit and associativity equations are those of $C$, coordinate by coordinate. Thus these formulas really define small simplicial categories and simplicial projection functors to the discrete simplicial category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Definitions 3.1.6–3.1.7 and 4.2.2; composition and empty input blocks.

proof.text: A finite product of Kan complexes is Kan by filling each coordinate of a horn; the empty product is a point. A coproduct of Kan complexes is Kan: every horn of positive dimension is nonempty and connected, so its map lands in one summand, where it can be filled. This includes empty mapping complexes, which have no horn maps. Consequently $P^\otimes$ and $D(C)$ are locally Kan. The coherent-nerve comparison makes their nerves quasicategories, identifies their mapping spaces naturally with the displayed enriched mapping complexes, and identifies the nerve of the discrete base with its ordinary nerve $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$. Each projected nerve map is an inner fibration: fill an inner horn in its quasicategorical total space; its projected filler is the prescribed base simplex because an inner horn in an ordinary nerve has a unique filler. Indeed that filler is the chain of its successive arrows with all other arrows their composites; for a two-dimensional inner horn it is precisely composition. Thus the relative lifting requirement follows without an additional fibration assumption.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.8 and Proposition 4.2.3(1); local Kan condition and inner lifting over the ordinary nerve.

proof.text: Let an inert arrow $[n]\to[m]$ be opposite to $\phi(j)=a+j$. For $c=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ take $c'=(c_{a+1},\ldots,c_{a+m})$ and the edge $e:c\to c'$ whose $m$ unary operations are identities. For a test list $z$ of length $\ell$ and $\psi:[\ell]\to[m]$, composition with $e$ identifies the $\psi$-summand of $P^\otimes(c',z)$ with the $\phi\psi$-summand of $P^\otimes(c,z)$: both are the product of operations on the blocks $c_{a+\psi(k-1)+1},\ldots,c_{a+\psi(k)}$. Therefore the square of enriched mapping complexes over the discrete sets of base arrows is a strict pullback. It is a homotopy pullback as well: paths in a discrete simplicial set are constant, so its path-space pullback equals its ordinary pullback. The natural, composition-compatible mapping-space comparison identifies this square with the mapping-space square in the coherent nerve; homotopy pullback invariance preserves the property under these equivalences of Kan spaces. Apply the cocartesian mapping criterion to conclude that $e$ is cocartesian. When $m=0$, the lift itself has no operation components. For a test list $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_\ell)$, the unique map $\psi:[\ell]\to[0]$ gives on both sides the product $\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}P(;z_k)$, since $\phi\psi$ is constant at $a$. This product can be empty and need not be a point; the identity between the two copies still gives the pullback. For $\ell=0$ it is the empty product, a point. Thus the calculation also supplies the required lifts to $[0]$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.8, expanded nonsymmetric inert-lift argument; compare Proposition 4.2.3(1), mapping-square argument.

proof.text: Let $U$ be the unary simplicial category of $P$. The strict enriched fiber of $P^\otimes$ at $[n]$ is $U^n$: only $\phi=\mathrm{id}_{[n]}$ is retained, and every resulting operation is unary. For $n=0$ this fiber has one object and its identity mapping point. The coherent nerve commutes with these fibers and products directly from its definition: an enriched functor from $\mathfrak C[\Delta^r]$ into a fiber is exactly an enriched functor with constant projection, and one into $U^n$ is an $n$-tuple of functors into $U$. The inert edges constructed above therefore give the Segal identification $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(P^\otimes)_{[n]}=(N_{\mathrm{hc}}U)^n$, and at $[1]$ give $N_{\mathrm{hc}}U$. For a source list $c$, target list $d$ of length $m$, and base arrow opposite to $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, projection to each target coordinate identifies its mapping space over this arrow with $\prod_{i=1}^m P(c_{\phi(i-1)+1},\ldots,c_{\phi(i)};d_i)$. This is the required mapping-space Segal map, since the $i$th factor is the mapping space over the composite with the inert projection to $d_i$. The base mapping space is discrete, so this enriched summand represents its homotopy fiber. Along with the inner fibration and inert lifts already proved, these are all three operad conditions. No condition that nullary operation spaces be nonempty or contractible has been introduced.

source.place: Definitions 3.1.3 and 3.1.7, Lemma 3.1.8; operadic fiber and mapping-space Segal conditions.

proof.text: For any $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ and $c=(c_0,\ldots,c_n)$ in $D(C)$, put $\phi_!c=(c_{\phi(0)},\ldots,c_{\phi(m)})$ and let $e_\phi:c\to\phi_!c$ have identity components. For a test string $z=(z_0,\ldots,z_\ell)$ and $\psi:[\ell]\to[m]$, precomposition with $e_\phi$ is the identity identification between $\prod_{k=0}^\ell C(c_{\phi\psi(k)},z_k)$ in the $\psi$-summand out of $\phi_!c$ and the same product in the $\phi\psi$-summand out of $c$. Explicitly, the pullback retains a pair consisting of $\psi$ and a tuple in the $\phi\psi$-summand; its inverse sends that pair to the same tuple in the $\psi$-summand. Distinct $\psi$ with equal $\phi\psi$ remain distinct because the pair retains $\psi$. Hence the mapping square is a strict pullback over discrete base mapping sets, and therefore a homotopy pullback by the constant-path calculation of step 3. Coherent-nerve mapping comparison and homotopy pullback invariance give the nerve mapping square; the cocartesian mapping criterion makes $e_\phi$ cocartesian. Such an edge exists for every string and every outgoing base arrow, so this projection is a cocartesian fibration.

The strict enriched fibre of $D(C)$ at $[n]$ is $C^{n+1}$, including $C$ at $[0]$, and the degreewise enriched-functor calculation of step 4 identifies its coherent nerve with $(N_{\mathrm{hc}}C)^{n+1}$. Transport along $\phi$ sends objects and all mapping simplices by $(c_j),(f_j)\mapsto(c_{\phi(i)}),(f_{\phi(i)})$; the selected lifts satisfy $e_\psi e_\phi=e_{\phi\psi}$ and $e_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3(2)–(4), Remark 4.1.2, and the explicit i^*⊣i_* plus fibrewise criterion route in Proposition 4.2.3(3)–(4); the n-fold exponent in the source proof is corrected to n+1 by Definition 4.2.2.

proof.text: Let $i:\{[0]\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the zeroth-simplex inclusion. The node [lem-coef-cocartesian-right-kan-extension-simplex-powers] supplies the right adjoint $i_*$ with $(i_*N_{\mathrm{hc}}C)_{[n]}=(N_{\mathrm{hc}}C)^{n+1}$, and its adjunction gives a canonical map $\Theta_C:N_{\mathrm{hc}}D(C)\to i_*N_{\mathrm{hc}}C=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{N_{\mathrm{hc}}C}$ over $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, natural in $C$ and preserving cocartesian edges. Since the adjunction equivalence is restriction to the fibres over $[0]$, $(\Theta_C)_{[0]}$ is the identity of $N_{\mathrm{hc}}C$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3(2)–(4), Remark 4.1.2, and the explicit i^*⊣i_* plus fibrewise criterion route in Proposition 4.2.3(3)–(4); the n-fold exponent in the source proof is corrected to n+1 by Definition 4.2.2.

proof.text: Let $\rho_j:[n]\to[0]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be opposite to the vertex $j:[0]\to[n]$. Because $\Theta_C$ preserves cocartesian edges, it carries the selected lift $e_{\rho_j}$ of step 5 to a cocartesian edge over $\rho_j$; hence the $j$th coordinate of $(\Theta_C)_{[n]}$, which by the right-Kan node is transport along $\rho_j$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{N_{\mathrm{hc}}C}$, is equivalent to $(\Theta_C)_{[0]}$ composed with transport along $\rho_j$ in $N_{\mathrm{hc}}D(C)$, i.e. to the $j$th projection $(c_0,\ldots,c_n)\mapsto c_j$. Thus on the fibre at $[n]$, $\Theta_C$ is equivalent to the map whose coordinates are the $n+1$ projections, i.e. to the identity of $(N_{\mathrm{hc}}C)^{n+1}$, and is an equivalence (this is the commutative square with the Segal maps in the source proof of (iv)).

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3(2)–(4), Remark 4.1.2, and the explicit i^*⊣i_* plus fibrewise criterion route in Proposition 4.2.3(3)–(4); the n-fold exponent in the source proof is corrected to n+1 by Definition 4.2.2.

proof.text: Both $N_{\mathrm{hc}}D(C)$ and $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{N_{\mathrm{hc}}C}$ are cocartesian fibrations over $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, i.e. fibrant objects of the cocartesian model structure of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] with their cocartesian edges marked, and $\Theta_C$ is a map between them; that node (opposite form) says such a map whose vertex-fibre maps are equivalences of quasicategories has a marked inverse over the base up to coherent natural equivalences over the base, so $\Theta_C$ is a categorical equivalence of total quasicategories. Under [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], this proves that the classifying functor is the coherent diagram $[n]\mapsto(N_{\mathrm{hc}}C)^{n+1}$ with its projection and diagonal transports, including the higher coherences supplied by the adjunction.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3(2)–(4), Remark 4.1.2, and the explicit i^*⊣i_* plus fibrewise criterion route in Proposition 4.2.3(3)–(4); the n-fold exponent in the source proof is corrected to n+1 by Definition 4.2.2.

proof.text: Now suppose $\pi_0C$ is a groupoid; this includes a locally Kan simplicial groupoid. The coherent-nerve comparison says $N_{\mathrm{hc}}C$ is Kan. Every strict fiber identified in step 6 is consequently Kan. Any edge $h:c\to d$ over $\phi$ factors as $c\xrightarrow{e_\phi}\phi_!c\xrightarrow{v}d$, with $v$ over the identity and its components exactly the components of $h$. Substitution in $D(C)$ gives a two-simplex witnessing this factorization in its nerve. The edge $v$ is an equivalence: it lies in a Kan fiber, where outer two-horn fillers give its inverse and inverse triangles. It remains an equivalence in the total space. The relative outer-horn lifting theorem implies that an equivalence edge of an inner fibration is cocartesian, because it fills precisely the required initial horns. The cocartesian composition theorem, applied to the displayed two-simplex, now makes $h$ cocartesian. Thus every edge is cocartesian. All initial horns in dimensions at least two lift by their first edge's cocartesianness; dimension-one initial horns lift using the edges $e_\phi$. Along with the inner horns this is exactly the left-fibration condition, including empty fibers.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3 and Remark 4.1.2, groupoidal specialization; explicit horn argument for the left-fibration conclusion.

proof.text: A simplicial multifunctor applies to each color and operation in the operator construction; a simplicial functor $F:C\to C\prime$ applies to every object and mapping simplex in a string. These maps commute strictly with the composition formulas of step 1 and with the selected identity-component lifts, because they preserve units and composition. Consequently the fiber identifications with powers are natural, as are the inert-lift and mapping-Segal identifications for the operator construction. For strings, the right-Kan adjunction of [lem-coef-cocartesian-right-kan-extension-simplex-powers] gives a natural comparison $\Theta_C$ of cocartesian fibrations, with a coherent natural square whose vertical maps are $N_{\mathrm{hc}}D(F)$ and $i_*N_{\mathrm{hc}}F$. Steps 8 and 9 prove that every $\Theta_C$ is an equivalence over the base. Naturality of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] therefore identifies these comparisons with an equivalence of the classifying coherent diagrams, including the projection and diagonal transitions. This supplies the asserted naturality with all higher coherences; no strict choice of the adjunction unit is required.

source.place: Definitions 3.1.7 and 4.2.2; Proposition 4.2.3(3)–(4), with naturality through i^*⊣i_* and the fibrewise-equivalence criterion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q51-61b4d15fe (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item, all 11 steps, the statement of each of the 12 cited nodes, and the unit and citer records. I also checked the source in Gepner–Haugseng arXiv:1312.3178 (PDF extracted locally): Def. 3.1.6–3.1.7, Lemma 3.1.8, Def. 4.1.1, Rem. 4.1.2/4.1.4, Def. 4.2.2 and Prop. 4.2.3(i)–(iv) with proof, pp. 20 and 36–38. Both displayed formulas match GH exactly, with GH's fibrant read as Kan / locally Kan. The source prints NC^{×n} in the proof of (iv); that is a typo for n+1 (Def. 4.2.2 and Rem. 4.1.2), and the node correctly uses n+1. The statement is unchanged and not weakened. I checked each step by hand. Steps 1–2: the block endpoints under substitution and the inner lifting over N(Δ^op) are correct. Steps 3 and 5: the inert and identity-component lifts give strict pullbacks over discrete Hom sets, including m=0, empty nullary operations and non-injective φ. Step 4: the mapping Segal map is literally the factor P(c_{φ(i-1)+1..φ(i)}; d_i), and n=0 gives a point fibre. Steps 7–9: these follow GH (iii)–(iv) using the restriction and projection clauses of the right-Kan node and the opposite form of the marked fibrewise criterion. Step 10: an edge factors as e_φ followed by a vertical equivalence; equivalence edges are cocartesian by the outer-horn tool, so the edge is cocartesian by the composition lemma, which gives the left fibration. Step 11 now claims only coherent naturality. I accept the tool use of lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift: it is a generic lemma, and no same-unit node states that equivalence edges are cocartesian. There are no new nodes. An rg search for the operator and string constructions found no duplicate, and there is no cycle. proof_deps matches the step uses, and no SGA is used. I made no changes.
